content:
The test image shows **split-open soybean stems** lying on dark soil. The stems are tan/dry externally, with dark internal discoloration and what appears to be small dark specks (possibly microsclerotia) inside.

**Plant part: stem.** Candidates: Anthracnose, Brown_Stem_Rot, Charcoal_Rot, Fusarium, Green_stem_disorder, Phytophthora, Rhizoctonia, Tobacco_Streak_Virus, White_Mold, and others.

Top suspects based on symptoms: **Charcoal_Rot** (microsclerotia), **Brown_Stem_Rot** (brown pith), **Phytophthora** (brown stem discoloration), **Fusarium** (brown vascular tissue).

Let me view reference images one per class, starting with these top candidates.
Charcoal_Rot reference shows gray streaking externally. Now let me check Brown_Stem_Rot.
BSR reference shows green stems with white pith and some browning - very different from the test image's dry, mature stems. Let me check Fusarium and Phytophthora.
Fusarium shows younger green plants - not matching. Now Phytophthora.

Phytophthora shows dark brown discoloration on living green stems - not matching the dry, mature split stems in the test image. Let me check White_Mold, Anthracnose, Rhizoctonia, and the other Charcoal_Rot reference.
White Mold shows fluffy white mold on green stems - not matching. Now Anthracnose and Rhizoctonia.
Rhizoctonia shows lesions on young green stems. Not matching. Let me view the second Charcoal_Rot reference to confirm my leading candidate.

This second Charcoal_Rot reference is very similar to the test image: dry stems split open with visible small dark specks (microsclerotia) giving the characteristic "charcoal-sprinkled" appearance.

**Analysis summary:**

The test image shows mature, dry soybean stems split lengthwise on dark soil. Key features:
- Tan/gray dry stems
- Dark internal discoloration in the pith
- Small dark granular specks (microsclerotia) visible inside the stem
- Characteristic "charcoal-sprinkled" or marbled internal appearance

This matches **Charcoal_Rot** perfectly. The microsclerotia in the vascular tissue and pith are the hallmark diagnostic feature. Other stem diseases were ruled out: BSR shows brown pith in green stems, Phytophthora shows chocolate-brown discoloration on living stems, White Mold shows fluffy white mycelium, Fusarium affects younger plants, Rhizoctonia shows cankers at soil line, and Anthracnose shows external dark lesions with acervuli.
